doe-osti-3362876-acrrf-high-bay-dose-cal:
Jeff Cardoni, Zackary Dodson, Jesse Phillips, and Zac Jankovsky of Sandia National Laboratories compute radiation doses in report SAND2026-20690, printed May 2026. The subject is the Annular Core Research Reactor facility high bay, the tall hall above the reactor. Part B covers the worst vertical beam paths: the unshielded central cavity, the FREC-II cavity, and the neutron radiography shaft. Results feed the facility safety basis, the document that bounds how the reactor may run.

Peak dose came to about 1,430 millirem per 300 megajoule pulse, or about 40,930 rem per hour at full power on the same scale. Mesh maps show how dose falls off across the bay. One warning stands out: setting objects over the central cavity, even a thin steel plate, can make the scattered field above it significantly worse.
doe-osti-3364003-laser-spectroscopy-of-e:
A final report to the DOE Office of Science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology closes award DE-SC0021179. The Early Career Research Program project was led by Ronald Fernando Garcia Ruiz from September 2020 to September 2025. The project used laser spectroscopy, shining tuned laser light on atoms to read their structure, to study exotic atoms and molecules built around actinide isotopes. These short-lived radioactive nuclei are predicted to be pear-shaped, a rare deformation called octupole deformation.

Pear-shaped nuclei amplify signals that would reveal new physics, such as violations of fundamental symmetries. The team produced and measured these fragile systems despite their scarcity and short lifetimes. Results map nuclear, atomic, and molecular structure across the isotopes studied. The work supports precision searches planned at current and future radioactive beam facilities.
doe-osti-3365512-development-of-composit:
University of California, Irvine's final report for DOE award DE-EE0008838, led by Shane Ardo with eight partner institutions, covers October 2019 to October 2023 work on photocatalysts that split water with sunlight. The target: particle suspensions that turn at least 10 percent of solar energy into hydrogen, the efficiency a practical dual-bed reactor needs to hit DOE cost goals. Perovskite oxide particles were the platform.

Strategies attacked the materials' light absorption and charge handling. Single-particle studies of rhodium-doped strontium titanate found a trap state 0.34 electron volts below the conduction band, matching the roughly 2.8 electron volt optical transition seen in luminescence. Heat-dependent transport tests on single nanoparticles tied the traps to oxygen vacancies. Partners from Columbia to Tokyo universities contributed reactor designs in the Z-scheme arrangement, where two photocatalysts split the water-splitting job.
doe-osti-3366323-macroalgae-cultivation-:
A technical progress report for ARPA-E award DE-AR0000920 covers the MACMODS macroalgae modeling project at the University of California, Irvine, led by Kristen Davis, from May 2018 to June 2024. MACMODS predicts how ocean seaweed farms grow and interact with currents, so farms can be sited and designed on evidence. The project was transferring to Stanford as the PI moved institutions.

Field observations ran at three farms, reaching 82 percent completion for that milestone, including the 86-acre Ocean Rainforest site offshore Santa Barbara in summer 2024. Model validation against farm growth data reached 95 percent. Published work shows kelp farms generating their own Langmuir circulations and pulling nutrients upward by turbulent mixing. A model-informed farm design paper appeared in June 2024.
doe-osti-3375395-proliferated-resilient-:
Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory report LLNL-TR-2019863, by John Cortes Gutierrez and dated June 2026, presents PREEMPT, a concept for swarms of small space telescopes. The name spells out Proliferated Resilient Economical Half-Meter Aperture Space Telescopes. Today's imaging payloads for spy and space-watch work can cost hundreds of millions of dollars. PREEMPT bets that many cheap half-meter scopes can do the same work. The project ran as an LDRD effort coded 23-ERD-052.

The team sorted its current monolithic optic against the new plan. It then drafted the V20 payload, a fifty-centimeter scope, as the next step. Runs of structural, shake, and heat tests flagged the main risks. The design looks workable, with heat control as the chief worry. Side work built a nonlinear model of Viton, the seal material at the optic mount, and showed printed metal composites can serve in a payload.
doe-osti-3387426-fast-1-2-2-a-computer-c:
FAST-1.2.2: A Computer Code for Thermal-Mechanical Nuclear Fuel Analysis under Steady-State and Transients, dated May 2026, is the manual for the FAST code. It was prepared for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's Office of Nuclear Regulatory Research. Six Pacific Northwest authors are printed, led by K. J. Geelhood, with J. Corson and J. J. Whitman of the commission. The code was developed under the NQA-1-2017 quality standard.

FAST computes how a fuel rod behaves in a running reactor. It tracks heat conduction through the pellet, mechanical strain, and coolant heating, in steady operation and transients. It uses a single-channel coolant enthalpy rise model. It uses a finite difference heat conduction model with mesh spacing finer at the pellet edge, where high-burnup fuel peaks in power. This volume covers structure, limits, model summaries, and input instructions. Companion volumes assess predictions against measured fuel data and document the MatLib models.
doe-osti-3409099-mechanical-electrochemi: Crash-testing an EV battery is expensive — simulating it is cheaper, if the model is right. Santhanagopalan and Lim's final report builds mechanical, electrochemical, and thermal models of EV batteries for crash simulation. The combined models predict how a battery bends, heats, and fails when metal meets metal.
doe-osti-3409100-mechanical-electrochemi:
Report NLR/TP-5700-100722 from the National Laboratory of the Rockies, dated August 2026, covers training on linked mechanical, electrical, and thermal battery models. Anudeep Mallarapu was the lab contact, with Jaeyoung Lim in the evidence record. The work ran under CRADA number CRD-19-00798.

One study used strain as the trigger for internal short circuit in a high-capacity cell. Voltage dropped sharply when that rule fired in the model. The team built and checked a combined model of the short inside a finite element tool. Trainees learn how a crush fault can turn into heat and failure inside a vehicle battery.
doe-osti-3626701-hanford-reach-fall-chin:
Hanford report HNF-73706, Revision 0, published in August 2026, tracks fall Chinook salmon spawning nests in the Hanford Reach for calendar year 2025. J. J. Nugent, C. T. Lindsey, and M. F. Paulsen of Hanford Mission Integration Solutions wrote it for the DOE Hanford Field Office. A redd is the gravel nest a salmon digs to lay eggs. Counting redds shows returning fish numbers.

Crews surveyed the reach from the air and digitized each redd they could see. Maps divide the river into upper, middle, and lower parts and plot redd density for 2025. Charts place the year in counts back to 1948 and link peak counts to estimated escapement from 1964 onward. Visibility had limits: nests in deep water or in thick clusters low in the reach were hard to see. Redds showed in water up to seven metres deep.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DrenasWilliamM_:
Officer J. D. Tippit was murdered in Dallas shortly after President Kennedy was shot, and his killing became a second crime at the center of that day. Bi Drenas built a research study of the Tippit murder titled Car #10, Where Are You? The study rests on the witnesses' own words.

Drenas questions the official investigation rather than repeating it. By working from testimony, the study lets each witness's account stand against the version the public was given. For readers of the Dallas evidence, it is a close, skeptical reading of the case that is often treated as settled.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GildayWilliamM_: Nsia-GildayWilliamM Gilday William M: the made public government document, captured as titled, subject: government records. A bare file, kept as issued, an obscure item, dated entry. From the archive shelves, for readers of the files.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-KingMartinLuthe:
Playbill, the theater program magazine, marked its fifteenth anniversary with an issue honoring Martin Luther King Jr. The issue features King's final published statement, A Testament of Hope. It also carries a feature called The Decent Society, taking its theme from King's own hopes for the country.

A theater magazine honoring a preacher shows how wide King's place in American culture had become. His last published words reached readers between the covers of a Broadway program book. The issue preserves that tribute whole, King's testament printed by an industry far from his pulpit.

On July 17, 1968, the Memphis Police Department's Inspectional Bureau issued a report on its security and surveillance of Martin Luther King Jr. Assistant Chief W. E. Routt wrote it. The report covers the period from King's arrival in Memphis on April 3 until his assassination there.

King had come to Memphis to support striking sanitation workers. The report records how the department watched and guarded him during those final days. As an internal police account written three months after the murder, it shows what the department said its own role had been. It also preserves the names, posts, and routines of the officers assigned to him.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MoranElizabethM: Elizabeth Moran: the garbled letter apparently addressed to 'Weisberg' - the substance is not recoverable. Damaged, but kept, complete. A single letter, filed. An obscure item. From the archive's collection, for researchers of the files and readers.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-RequestForMoney: Harold Weisberg wrote this letter to a member of the House of Representatives. It concerns the House Select Committee on Assassinations, which was then reinvestigating the King and Kennedy murders. The file's own label ties it to a request made in 1978. Weisberg's letters to Congress usually asked for records, oversight, or help with agencies. The file does not name the member or summarize this letter, so its specific request cannot be stated.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-TurnerFayM_Turn: Fay M. Turner testified before the Warren Commission about what he heard on the day of the Kennedy assassination. Questioned by commission lawyer Mr. Belin, he gave his account under oath. The commission questioned hundreds of witnesses this way in 1964. Turner's testimony is one voice in that large record, preserved so readers can weigh what bystanders said they saw and heard in Dallas.
govdocs-archive_org-the-viking-king-of-p: Jacques de Mahieu claimed that Vikings reached South America long before Columbus. The Viking King of Paraguay tells his account of alleged Norse settlement in Paraguay. Mainstream historians reject such claims for lack of evidence. The library holds the book as an archive item, without backing, and classes it as fringe history. It serves the study of diffusionist theories: bold stories about ancient voyages that evidence has not confirmed.
nasa-tm-19640018170-effect-of-compressib:
M. P. Singh of Goddard Space Flight Center's theoretical division wrote this paper. It studies drag on a ball that vibrates in a special fluid. The fluid conducts electricity, is thick, and can be compressed. Rotation and a magnetic field act on the flow as well.

Singh's introduction ties the math to motions inside Earth itself. Flow in Earth's liquid core may make the planet's magnetic field, he notes. Spinning forces and magnetic forces there interact in complex ways. The near match of geographic and magnetic poles hints at spin's strong role. His vibrating ball is a clean model for forces that also shape planets and stars.
nasa-tm-19650014109-coriolis-effects-dur:
John D Stewart and Brant Clark studied a subtle effect on pilots inside a moving flight simulator. When the cab pitches or rolls, extra forces act on the balance organs in the inner ear. Those forces can make a pilot feel motion that is not really happening. The study used the Ames five-degree-of-freedom simulator.

Three modes of simulator motion were tested. The authors looked at strong Coriolis effects and at false feelings of position in space. Such illusions matter, because a pilot who misreads motion may react wrongly. Knowing where the illusion starts helps designers keep simulator training honest and safe.
nasa-tm-19680011015-photomeson-productio:
F. W. Stecker, at the Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, reopens a cosmic ray question in February 1968. Very energetic cosmic rays should lose energy by making mesons when they strike the universe's microwave glow. Many expected the cosmic ray spectrum to fall off sharply at the top for that reason.

Stecker reexamines that photomeson effect on the high-energy spectrum. His reexamination leads to a softer conclusion. The spectrum, he finds, may not steepen abruptly at high energy after all. The result mattered for how far the most energetic cosmic rays can travel before the microwave background robs their energy.
nasa-tm-19690028198-summary-of-particle-: James I. Vette of Goddard Space Flight Center sums up particle groups in the magnetosphere in this September 1969 preprint, numbered X-614-69-313. Trapped electrons and protons fill the zone around Earth in belts. Those belts can harm spacecraft and crews. The report record describes the mean behavior of those groups over time. A summary like this gives planners base levels for radiation risk. The hosted sample holds the cover page only, after a modern copy notice. No group values can be stated from the sample.
nasa-tm-19700026567-vacuum-deposition-of:
Vacuum deposition of semiconductor materials is the subject of this report from the Manned Spacecraft Center in Houston. The materials belong to the 3-5 family, named for the columns of their elements. The work uses the three-temperature deposition method to lay them down as films for thin film transistor work.

The work grew out of a summer faculty fellowship program and centers on indium antimonide films. Indium and antimony were laid down together in vacuum to form the compound film. Measured mobility in those films ran well above the values of films then in common use. The authors detail their procedures, note the gain over cadmium selenide films, and recommend directions for future work.
nasa-tm-19720017873-mechanical-propertie:
William D Klopp and Walter R Witzke of the Lewis Research Center reported these alloy tests in June 1972, as NASA TM X-2576. They studied molybdenum melted by electron beam, plus three dilute molybdenum rhenium alloys. Pure molybdenum turns brittle at low temperatures, which limits its use. Small rhenium additions were known to help tungsten greatly. The study asked whether the same trick worked for molybdenum, and measured the strength effects.

All three alloys stayed ductile to colder temperatures than the pure metal. The richest alloy improved the changeover point by about two hundred degrees Celsius. Rhenium also raised tensile strength at low and high heat. High temperature creep strength rose as well. The pattern matched what dilute tungsten rhenium alloys had shown earlier.
new-york-times-current-history-the-europ:
May 1915 forms number two of volume two in the New York Times Current History of the European War. The magazine ran from April to September 1915, with an index. General Sir John French tells his own story in this number, with a map.

French's account centres on the costly victory of Neuve Chapelle. Sidney Low's poem Roberts of Kandahar follows the general's report. Another long piece tells how Przemysl, Galicia's strong fortress, yielded to a Russian siege, with maps. A poem called The Jesters lightens the run of battle reports. The number mixes commanders' words, verse, and siege news for American readers at home.
pantheism-its-story-and-significance-rel: J. Allanson Picton's Pantheism: Its Story and Significance belongs to a popular series. The series is Religions Ancient and Modern. Each small volume cost one shilling net. The hosted sample shows the series advertisement only. Jane Harrison's Religion of Ancient Greece appears in it. Edward Clodd's Animism and H. A. Giles's Religions of Ancient China appear too. Volumes on Islam, Buddhism, and Hinduism were in preparation. No page of Picton's own argument appears in the sample.
podcast-dannyjones--y7DDPR2L-M:
Steve-O built his fame on Jackass, performing stunts that repeatedly put his body, and sometimes his life, at risk. Sitting with Danny Jones, he talks about the other side of that life: God, near-death experiences, and his own cheerful conviction that he is probably going to hell.

The tone swings between confession and comedy, which suits a guest whose career mixed both. Steve-O reflects on survival, addiction and recovery form the background of his story, and faith arrived late in it. Jones gives him room to be serious without sanding off the humor. The episode works as a celebrity interview with real weight, because the man describing brushes with death has had more of them than almost any guest on the show.
podcast-joerogan-t8h3-c-sJ-M:
Amanda Feilding, the British researcher who founded the Beckley Foundation, talks psychedelics and the ego in this Joe Rogan Experience segment. Feilding spent decades funding careful science on drugs that most labs avoided. Her foundation backed studies on LSD, cannabis, and consciousness itself.

Feilding explains how psychedelics can loosen the ego, the tight sense of self that runs daily life. She connects that effect to possible help for depression and addiction. Rogan asks about her own long, unusual path in science and policy. The segment gives drug research a patient, scholarly voice rarely heard on the show.
podcast-tuckercarlson-PpF26prP0_M:
Country star Jason Aldean joins Tucker Carlson for a heartfelt talk about fame and fire. Aldean was on stage during the Las Vegas mass shooting. That night still shapes his life and music.

He tells what he saw and how he coped after the attack. The title also names school policy on gender and fights inside country music. Aldean defends his small-town anthem and the backlash it drew. Carlson draws out a star who refuses to bend. The episode suits country fans who want the man behind the songs, unfiltered.
rogozhin-diela-moskovskoi-tsenzury-v-tsa: Diela Moskovskoi tsenzury v tsarstvovanie Pavla I, by Rogozhin. The Moscow censorship. This book preserves that study. Writers of history may cite it later. The paper lasts as a quiet witness. Time has kept the file intact.
shakespearean-tragedy-lectures-on-hamlet:
A. C. Bradley, formerly professor of poetry at Oxford, published these lectures on four great tragedies with Macmillan. A first edition came in 1904; this second edition of 1919 marks the thirteenth impression. Bradley treats Hamlet, Othello, King Lear, and Macbeth in turn.

Lecture by lecture, Bradley traces character, plot, and the moral world each play builds. His readings set the terms for a century of talk on Shakespearean tragedy. Students still meet Hamlet's delay and Lear's storm through Bradley's lens, even when they argue with it, since few critics have matched his care or his reach.
studies-in-the-psychology-of-sex-volume-:
Volume I of Havelock Ellis's Studies in the Psychology of Sex, in the 1927 printing, holds three studies: The Evolution of Modesty, The Phenomena of Sexual Periodicity, and Auto-Erotism. Ellis's general preface traces the work to his youth, spent partly in an Australian city and partly in the solitude of the bush.

There, he says, a resolve grew in him that a main part of his life's work should be to make the problems of sex clear. An earlier book, Man and Woman, served as his introduction to the ground. The studies that follow treat shame, rhythm, and self-love as natural facts to be mapped with care rather than as sins to be hushed.
the-myths-of-the-new-world-a-treatise-on:
Daniel G. Brinton's The Myths of the New World was published in 1868. Leypoldt and Holt issued it in New York, and Trubner and Company in London.
